title: R' Peringori of Caesarea

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Terumot, at the supplied 1:2 [compare 11:2]: ‘R' Peringori; Rabbi Lazar bei Rabbi Yishmael said.’ Hyman cites Nazir 7:2 for the same reading. Hyman says one should read, ‘R' Lazar, son of R' Yishmael, said.’

notes.text: The literal heading has Peringori (פרינגורי); the metadata omits the nun. The source juxtaposes Peringori and Lazar without spelling out their reporting relationship. Hyman replaces bei with a father-son formula.

The saved whole Venice Terumot11:2 scalar has abbreviated R' Perigori of Caesarea followed by full Rabbi Lazar bei Rabbi Yishmael. Supplied1:2 remains beside the11:2 match; no lost-yod print history follows. Source Peringori and named Perigori spellings stay distinct. Hyman’s one should read changes bei to the son-of formula, but does not explicitly settle whether preceding Peringori is also affected. Nazir7:2 was not newly inspected; its titles remain abbreviated. Search snippets of a different proposed correction are not an admitted commentary witness.

Both occurrences in the photographed Hyman notice read Perigori (פריגורי). Peringori (פרינגורי) is the spelling in the supplied transcription retained here. The print cites Terumot 1:2 and Nazir 7:2. In the passage located at Terumot 11:2, both consulted editions read Lazar bei Yishmael. In the parallel discussion at Nazir 6:2, the Venice text reads “son of Yishmael” and Guggenheimer reads “like Rabbi Yishmael.” That parallel does not name Perigori and leaves Hyman’s intended correction open.
